commits.edited_message:
[ttvarc] Factor out common code.

The 'VARC' table has four CFF2-style INDEX structures that were each parsed
by a separate hand-rolled copy; the missing offset-value validation that
caused the recent crashes had to be fixed in each copy independently.
Factor the parsing and bounds checking into a helper function and route all
four call sites through it.

The component axis-value stack buffer also always holds exactly
VARC_STACK_AXIS_COUNT entries, so select it by that constant directly.

* src/truetype/ttvarc.c (tt_varc_read_cff2_index_entry): New function.
  (tt_varc_get_glyph_record, tt_varc_parse_component,
  tt_varc_get_axis_indices): Use it.
  (tt_varc_read_index2_data): Remove, superseded by the helper function.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.edited_message:
* src/truetype/ttvarc.c (tt_varc_get_axis_indices): Fix zeros decoding.

A TupleValues "zeros" run decodes to zero values, matching HarfBuzz
(`TupleValues::decompile`, which memsets the run to 0) and fontTools; the
code instead wrote the running index (`indices[i] = i`), so a zeros run of
length two or more overrode the wrong axes.  No test font exercises it (they
use runs of length one, where 0 == i).

Also bound the run reads by the entry's own `tuple_limit` rather than the
whole-table `table_limit`, so a run straddling the entry end no longer
decodes bytes from adjacent entries (matches the counting pass in
`tt_varc_parse_component`).

Since a one-byte zeros run can now inflate the axis count to 64, cap the
axis-value stack buffer in `tt_face_load_varc_glyph` at 32 entries and let
larger counts use the heap, reducing the per-component stack footprint.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling: The defect is a stack-buffer-overflow (WRITE, CWE-787) in tt_varc_parse_component (src/truetype/ttvarc.c), reached through the public API FT_New_Memory_Face + FT_Load_Glyph on an in-spec TrueType font with a 'VARC' table. It is split across the two commits as a producer/consumer disagreement about the geometry of the caller's axis-value stack buffer. Commit b163093a0 ('[ttvarc] Factor out common code.') makes the callee tt_varc_parse_component choose the caller's stack buffer by the VARC_STACK_AXIS_COUNT constant (64) instead of the passed axis_values_buffer_size parameter. Read alone this is exact behavior-preserving refactoring: at that commit the sole caller declares FT_Fixed stack_axis_values[VARC_STACK_AXIS_COUNT] and passes VARC_STACK_AXIS_COUNT, so constant and parameter always agree (verified: a tree with only this edit runs the PoC clean). Commit b3ec921f7 ('* src/truetype/ttvarc.c (tt_varc_get_axis_indices): Fix zeros decoding.') shrinks that same caller-side buffer to 32 entries and passes 32, motivated by its own change (a one-byte TupleValues zeros run can now inflate axis_count to 64) to reduce per-component stack footprint. Read alone this is safe: the real callee honors the passed buffer size and sends counts > 32 to the heap (verified: a tree with only this edit also runs the PoC clean). Only the composition is buggy: after both commits the callee selects the stack path whenever axis_count <= 64 while the buffer it receives holds just 32 entries. For 33 <= axis_count <= 64 the axis-value fill loop in tt_varc_parse_component writes up to 64 FT_Fixed values into a 32-entry stack array of the caller tt_face_load_varc_glyph (stack-buffer-overflow WRITE at ttvarc.c:843, ASan abort rc 134 on the resulting tree; the original batch, the main base, and each single-edit tree all run the identical PoC clean, rc 0). A correct fix is therefore necessarily non-local: fixing commit 1 alone (e.g. reverting to the parameter) or commit 2 alone (e.g. restoring the 64-entry array, or growing the passed size) each removes the abort on its own only because each side independently re-establishes agreement; what a reviewer must actually recognize is that the callee's capacity assumption (VARC_STACK_AXIS_COUNT) and the caller's allocation (32) are defined in two different commits and have silently diverged - any fix that does not reconcile the callee's bound with the caller's actual buffer geometry across both diffs leaves the write reachable. The PoC font supplies axis_count = 64 via a one-byte zeros run (0xBF) in the axis-indices tuple plus a one-byte TupleValues run of 64 values in the component record, both within a well-formed VARC table, so the input is in-contract for the public rendering API.
